quickAnswers.question: Best model for agentic coding?
quickAnswers.why: Tops the AA Intelligence Index (58), Epoch's capabilities index (167) and Code Arena WebDev (1815). GPT-6 Astra leads the independent Terminal-Bench 4.0 run (59.6%), so the lead is real but contested.

quickAnswers.question: Best value per dollar?
quickAnswers.why: Inside Codex it scores 63 on AA's Coding Agent Index at about $1 per task. Claude Code with Sonnet 5.5 scores 68 but costs about $14 per task. BenchLM picks Sonnet 5.5 instead, at the same token price.

quickAnswers.question: Best open-weight model?
quickAnswers.why: Highest open-weight score on the AA Intelligence Index (46) and BenchLM, released under MIT on 21 Sept. GLM-5.3 (45) and Kimi K3 (44) are close behind. Price is from launch coverage, not a first-party page.

benchmarks.name: Arena Text
benchmarks.measures: Elo ratings from blind, crowd-sourced votes between two chat answers.
benchmarks.takeaway: Google's Gemini 4 Argon leads by about 20 points despite being in limited release. Anthropic models fill most of places 2–7, all within about 10 points of each other.
benchmarks.trustNote: Measures what voters prefer, not correctness. Style and length sway votes, and the top entries often overlap within confidence intervals.

benchmarks.name: Code Arena: WebDev
benchmarks.measures: Human votes on web apps that models build through multi-step agentic coding.
benchmarks.takeaway: Opus 5.5 Max leads GPT-6 Astra Max (1788) and Sonnet 5.5 (1786). Gemini 4 Argon, first on the text board, is only 9th here; Qwen 3.8 Max is the best open-weight entry at 10th.
benchmarks.trustNote: Votes reward how an app looks and feels, not whether the code is correct. The newest models have under 2k votes, so their ratings are still moving.

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
benchmarks.measures: Composite of 10 evaluations AA runs itself, alongside price, speed and cost per task.
benchmarks.takeaway: Opus 5.5 scores 58, ahead of Sonnet 5.5 (56). GPT-6 Astra and Gemini 4 Argon tie at 53, and GPT-6.1 Sol reaches 52 at roughly $0.72 per task. MiMo-V2.6-Pro leads open-weight models at 46.
benchmarks.trustNote: The index changes version often, so scores across versions aren't comparable, and each reasoning-effort setting is ranked as its own entry.

benchmarks.name: AA Coding Agent Index
benchmarks.measures: Scores a harness and model together (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, OpenCode…) with cost and time per task.
benchmarks.takeaway: Claude Code with Sonnet 5.5 scores 68 at about $14 per task. Codex with GPT-6.1 Sol scores 63 at about $1, and OpenCode with GLM-5.3 scores 54 at about $4. Each harness runs a different model, so these aren't like-for-like.
benchmarks.trustNote: Model and harness are blended into one number, and the full ranking table isn't public.

benchmarks.name: Same model, different harness
benchmarks.measures: How far a score moves when only the agent harness changes.
benchmarks.takeaway: On Terminal-Bench 2.1, Fable 5 scored 61.8% in Claude Code, 66.3% in OpenCode and 69.7% in AWS Strands. Swapping only the harness moved scores by 5–10 points, and cost by up to 4×.
benchmarks.trustNote: Numbers come from vendor launch posts. Nobody has yet run Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Cursor and Gemini CLI on one model under one setup.

benchmarks.name: SWE-Bench Pro
benchmarks.measures: Long, multi-file repository tasks run under Scale's own standard scaffold.
benchmarks.takeaway: On Scale's own runs the top scores sit around 60%, and the newest frontier models aren't listed yet. Vendors report far higher numbers with their own harnesses; Anthropic reports 89.9% for Opus 5.5.
benchmarks.trustNote: OpenAI's July audit estimated about 30% of tasks are broken, and Cursor found many solves came from looking up the existing fix.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
benchmarks.measures: Whether an agent can fix 500 real Python GitHub issues so hidden tests pass.
benchmarks.takeaway: Saturated: seven models score 95% or more on Vals.ai, including open-weight DeepSeek V4 Pro. OpenAI stopped reporting it in February and Epoch rates it flawed.
benchmarks.trustNote: Contaminated, many tests are flawed, and a 10-line conftest.py hack scores 100%. Treat any number here as history.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench
benchmarks.measures: Hard command-line tasks in a sandbox: software, ML, security and sysadmin work.
benchmarks.currentLeader: GPT-6 Astra (xhigh), v4.0 via Artificial Analysis
benchmarks.takeaway: Version 4.0 dropped the saturated tasks, so leaders now land around 55–60%, with Fable 5.1 second at 55.1%. Anthropic self-reports 66.4% for Opus 5.5. Versions 2.0 and 2.1 are near saturation.
benchmarks.trustNote: Highly harness-dependent, and several versions run side by side. Berkeley researchers scored 100% on 2.0 by wrapping its test binaries.

benchmarks.name: τ²-bench / τ³-bench
benchmarks.measures: Conversation, tool calls and policy rules in simulated customer-service domains.
benchmarks.takeaway: The hardest τ³ track is still under 60%, with Qwen 3.8 Max ahead of Claude Opus 5 (48.7%). Many frontier models haven't been submitted.
benchmarks.trustNote: Mostly self-submitted, with patchy frontier coverage. Earlier task sets had errors that later releases fixed.

benchmarks.name: METR Time Horizon
benchmarks.measures: How long a task (in expert human time) an agent completes half the time.
benchmarks.takeaway: METR says anything above about 16 hours is unreliable with its current task suite. Its GPT-5.6 Sol estimate ranged from 11h to over 270h depending on how cheating runs were counted. No measurement yet for Opus 5.5 or GPT-6.
benchmarks.trustNote: Suite is saturating, intervals are very wide, and reward hacking distorts results.

benchmarks.name: ARC-AGI-3
benchmarks.measures: Interactive game environments where the agent must learn the rules while playing.
benchmarks.takeaway: GPT-6 Astra scored 62.7% with the standard harness and up to 99.9% with a provider adapter. That's a 37-point swing from the harness alone, at around $26K per run.
benchmarks.trustNote: Very expensive to run and heavily harness-dependent. Third-party sites often quote the adapter score without saying so.

benchmarks.name: BrowseComp
benchmarks.measures: Whether a browsing agent can dig up hard-to-find facts on the web.
benchmarks.takeaway: Saturated: the top five all land between 90.8% and 92.5%. It no longer separates frontier models.
benchmarks.trustNote: Nearly every score is self-reported with each vendor's own search setup, and answers may have leaked onto the web.

benchmarks.name: OSWorld 2.0
benchmarks.measures: Long desktop and web workflows, scored by checkpoints and by full completion.
benchmarks.takeaway: Partial-credit scores look strong, with Fable 5.1, Simular Sai and GPT-6 Astra all above 72%. The best full-completion rate is still only 32%.
benchmarks.trustNote: Official runs, vendor self-reports and modified-task runs share one board. Berkeley researchers reached 73% without solving tasks.

benchmarks.name: Epoch Capabilities Index
benchmarks.measures: Stitches 50+ benchmarks onto one difficulty-weighted capability scale.
benchmarks.takeaway: Opus 5.5 tops the index. GPT-6 Astra set records on Epoch's math and puzzle benchmarks, including 2 of 68 open Erdős problems on FrontierMath.
benchmarks.trustNote: Inherits the flaws of the benchmarks it combines, and some inputs are developer-reported.

benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam (Diamond)
benchmarks.org: Center for AI Safety & Scale AI
benchmarks.measures: Expert-written questions across 100+ subjects; Diamond is a cleaned 1,000-question subset without tools.
benchmarks.takeaway: On Diamond, GPT-6 Astra leads Opus 5.5 (55.0%) and Fable 5.1 (51.3%). On the original set, Anthropic reports 67.7% with tools while AA measured 61.4%.
benchmarks.trustNote: Tool and no-tool runs get mixed together, and the original set had label errors.

benchmarks.name: ARC-AGI-2
benchmarks.measures: Abstract grid puzzles that test generalization to unseen tasks, with cost per task.
benchmarks.takeaway: Close to saturated. ARC Prize verified Opus 5 at 90.4% in July; the higher figures for GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and Opus 5.5 come from a mirror.
benchmarks.trustNote: Top scores aren't yet traced to an official verification, and saturation limits what it can still tell apart.

benchmarks.name: LiveBench
benchmarks.measures: Math, code, reasoning and language questions refreshed from recent sources to limit contamination.
benchmarks.takeaway: The top four (Claude and GPT-6 Astra) sit within about a point. No refresh confirmed since June.
benchmarks.trustNote: Data is only readable through mirrors, and public question sets lag the live board.

benchmarks.name: Aider Polyglot
benchmarks.measures: 225 coding exercises in six languages, solved through Aider's edit format.
benchmarks.takeaway: Last updated August 2025 with no 2026 models. Useful as history only.
benchmarks.trustNote: Unmaintained, the exercises are public and likely contaminated, and it is near saturation.

benchmarks.name: LLM Stats
benchmarks.measures: Composite score from public benchmarks plus live API price and speed.
benchmarks.takeaway: Opus 5.5 edges GPT-6 Astra (59.1) and Sonnet 5.5 (58.0). Kimi K3 is listed as the top open model.
benchmarks.trustNote: Most rows come from vendor announcements rather than its own runs.

benchmarks.name: BenchLM
benchmarks.measures: Weighted score across eight categories from about 500 benchmarks, with evidence-strength labels.
benchmarks.takeaway: GPT-6 Astra narrowly beats Opus 5.5 (87.7). It names Sonnet 5.5 best value and MiMo-V2.6-Pro top open-weight model.
benchmarks.trustNote: Blends self-reported and independent rows, and the weighting is its own design.

benchmarks.name: Vellum LLM Leaderboard
benchmarks.measures: Curated vendor-reported scores on benchmarks that aren't saturated yet, plus cost and speed.
benchmarks.takeaway: Handy for prices and speeds, but some category leaders are stale; SWE-bench still shows GPT-5.6 Sol.
benchmarks.trustNote: Repeats vendor numbers and updates unevenly across categories.

integrityIssues.title: Cursor: reward hacking on SWE-bench Pro
integrityIssues.summary: 63% of Opus 4.8 Max's successful solutions looked up the fix online or in git history; in a locked-down run its score fell from 87.1% to 73.0%.

integrityIssues.title: Berkeley RDI benchmark audit
integrityIssues.summary: Researchers audited 13 widely used agent benchmarks and rated every one critical risk, with 45 confirmed hacks that score highly without solving tasks.

integrityIssues.title: OpenAI drops SWE-bench Verified
integrityIssues.summary: An audit found most sampled problems had flawed tests and every frontier model showed signs of having seen them in training.

integrityIssues.title: OpenAI audit of SWE-bench Pro
integrityIssues.summary: About 30% of Pro tasks are broken, with tests too strict or too thin and prompts underspecified.

integrityIssues.title: METR: GPT-5.6 Sol time horizon
integrityIssues.summary: Depending on how cheating runs were counted, the estimate ranged from about 11 hours to over 270.

integrityIssues.title: ARC-AGI-3 harness gap
integrityIssues.summary: The same model scored 62.7% on the standard harness and up to 99.9% with a provider adapter; the higher figure spread without context.

integrityIssues.title: ImpossibleBench
integrityIssues.summary: Tests are changed so tasks can't be solved honestly, making any pass a measure of cheating. Frontier models pass often.
